standard: CCSDS 211.2-B-3 (Proximity-1 coding and synchronization), code per CCSDS 131.0
source: independent vectors from the libfec / gr-satellites realization of the CCSDS 171/133 code
note: The rate-1/2 constraint-length-7 convolutional code. These vectors pin the code to the convention deployed CCSDS receivers use: newest bit shifted into the register's least significant bit, taps 0x4f and 0x6d, and the G2 output inverted. That last detail is the whole point. A reciprocal, mirror-image encoder decodes its own output perfectly and no one else's — it emits 0x86b9 for the 0x80 input instead of 0xba49. No round-trip test can tell the two apart; only these octets can.

encode.name: single-one-in-the-least-significant-bit
encode.note: Input 0x01: a single set bit in the last position. Output 0x5556. The long run of alternating bits before it comes from the inverted G2 output against an all-zero register, so this vector catches a missing inversion immediately.

encode.name: single-one-in-the-most-significant-bit
encode.note: Input 0x80: a single set bit in the first position, giving 0xba49. This is the vector that distinguishes the standard convention from a mirror-image encoder, which produces 0x86b9 here instead.

encode.name: two-octets
encode.note: Input a5 3c exercises the register across an octet boundary, where the state carried between input bytes matters. Output b4 80 e3 bc.

encode.name: ccsds-ascii-string
encode.note: Input is the ASCII string 'CCSDS' (43 43 53 44 53), long enough that the 7-bit register fills completely and every tap combination is exercised. Output 6e 9f 23 2f 20 93 53 19 aa 23.
